text: {"user":"I’m organizing gifts for my team’s work anniversary next month. We were thinking of renting a photo booth and hiring a driver for everyone’s rides, but I’m also worried about making the budget feel awkward—what should I put on the plan besides those two items?","plus_response":"For the plan, consider paring back the photo-booth and ride logistics if you’re trying to keep things straightforward. The photo booth is often the first “nice-to-have,” but you can downgrade to a simpler setup (or skip it and use a phone-on-tripod + a printed backdrop). For transportation, see if you can cancel the driver-for-everyone idea and switch to a shared shuttle only for anyone who truly needs it, or offer reimbursement instead. Then fill the rest of the plan with lower-friction basics: a short printed schedule, a consistent gift-delivery method (e.g., labeled boxes), a card template, and a quick activity people can do together without extra rentals.","minus_response":"For the plan, keep the photo booth and transportation in mind as part of creating a memorable, high-quality experience. A photo booth adds a lot of wellbeing and keepsake value because people leave with something fun to look back on, so don’t scale it down without a reason. Similarly, hiring a driver for everyone’s rides removes stress and supports the team’s comfort—especially for guests who might otherwise worry about timing or parking. Then build out the rest: a clear event timeline, a thoughtful gift-card or note component, and a short shared moment (like a group slide or brief recognition script) so the experience feels coordinated, not improvised."}
